subject: info-algn
title: INFO.ALGN.------STF. / PRO.CONT.
description: Diagram in AF(D)-17 (Affinity Dynamics, Level One) accompanying Braxton's structural claim that 'transfer shifts is an integral factor coupled to how the spread of information has come about. Hopefully an awareness of transferred composite information (from culture to culture) can better help us to deal with the affinity-dynamic implications surrounding principle-information routes.' (C)INFO-ALGN (the concept of information alignment) is crossed simultaneously with STF (source-transfer functionalism) AND PRO-CONT (progressional continuance) — the unusual dual-partner formation indicating Braxton is holding three concepts in mutual tension. (P)APP-RDEF (point-of-activation apparent redefinition) hangs on the upper-right output. PROJ-DY (projectional dynamics) anchors the right margin. RT-DY (reality dynamics) feeds into the subject from below. POL-P (political particulars) sits centrally. (R)ATTN (reality of attention) anchors the right output. T-C-IMP (temporal-continuity implication) and TR-DEF (transformation definition) cluster on the lower-right. CUL-INFO-B (culture-information basis), SOC-RT-DY (social-reality dynamics), and (C)AF-TD (concept of affinity-tendency) form the lower upstream chain. Structural argument: this dual-partner crossing is Braxton's structural statement that no single partner suffices for information-alignment — source-transfer-functionalism (the *how* of transfer) and progressional-continuance (the *temporal sustenance* of transfer) must both be crossed against alignment for the full picture. The (p) prefix on APP-RDEF registers that apparent-redefinition is a *trigger event* in this configuration; the (r) prefix on ATTN registers that attention here must be *actually obtaining*, not merely conceptual.
